title: What is known about 1RB1LE_0RC0RB_1RD1RF_1LA0LE_0LD0LB_---0RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_0RC0RB_1RD1RF_1LA0LE_0LD0LB_---0RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

The tape is a sequence of copies of 110 separated by short gaps (0, 000 or 1 00), in no visible order, and the run keeps rewriting it. It grows on both sides, by about 100 cells per tenfold increase in time.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 1010 steps.

Where a halt would come from. The machine halts only in state F reading 0, and F is entered only from C reading 1 and stepping right (1RF). In the first 108 steps that happens 5,555,291 times and F always reads a 1.

Why it is hard. No counter or repeating cycle has shown up: macro machines with blocks of 2 to 6 cells do not compress the run (with blocks of k cells, about one macro step per k steps), and the contents of the tape look irregular. A finite-automaton invariant (CTL) with windows of up to 8 cells does not close. A proof would need an invariant that captures why the halting pattern never forms, and none is known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 576 cells have been visited and 281 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Slow, irregular growth
claims.text: Cells visited (from the C simulator's records): 239 at 10<sup>6</sup>, 316 at 10<sup>7</sup>, 462 at 10<sup>8</sup>, 575 at 10<sup>9</sup>, 672 at 10<sup>10</sup> steps. The tape grows by a roughly constant number of cells per factor of 10 in time.

claims.title: The halting pattern never forms
claims.text: F is entered only from C reading 1 (1RF). In the first 108 steps that happens 5,555,291 times and F reads a 1 every time.

claims.title: No macro structure found
claims.text: Macro machines with blocks of 3 and 6 cells take about one macro step per 3, respectively 6 to 7, steps over 107 steps (bbtools.macro), so the run has no long uniform stretches for a shift rule to cross; the accelerator bbtools.cycles (blocks of 4) finds no linear cycle in 107 steps.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.16).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The run looks chaotic on a slowly growing tape; no structure that would rule out the halting pattern has been found.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine stirs a small tape in an irregular way, growing it only a few cells at a time. This page runs the real machine in your browser and lists what is known.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Visited after 10<sup>10</sup> steps; about logarithmic growth.
No counter, cycle or macro structure found.

sections.heading: An irregular, slowly growing tape
html: Read the tape with b = 110. At step 909,086,155, when the tape grows on the right, it begins
1 0 0 1 b 0 b 0^4 b 1 0 0 b 0^3 b 0^3 b 0 b 0 b 0^3 b 0^3 b 1 0 0 b …
and goes on like that for 575 cells: 110s with gaps of 0s, irregularly arranged. Width: 239 cells at 106 steps, 462 at 108, 672 at 1010.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The machine halts only in state F reading 0, and F is entered only from C reading 1 and stepping right (1RF). In the first 108 steps that happens 5,555,291 times and F always reads a 1.

For a run this irregular, the honest summary is that it behaves like a random process on a tape that grows very slowly, with one forbidden pattern that has never appeared. Whether something forbids it, or it is only unlikely, is not known.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.16).
After 109 steps the tape spans 576 cells (174 left of the start, 393 right), with a density of 1s of 0.488.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Stirs a tape of 110 words separated by 0, 000 or 100 in an irregular way; grows about 100 cells per tenfold time.
